situation.text: Hoje você conhece Nina, de San Francisco. Comprar um cartão de transporte.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende o dinheiro em espécie: coins (moedas), bills (notas) e change (troco).

pages.hook: Many American cities have a reloadable card for buses and trains. You add money once, then you just tap the card and go.
pages.polite: Staff often ask **“How much do you want to add?”** You can answer with just the amount.

mythfact.s: San Francisco Bay Area transit uses a card called Clipper.
mythfact.why: Clipper works on buses, trains and ferries around the Bay.

mythfact.s: Every US city uses the same transit card.
mythfact.why: Each region has its own card, like SmarTrip in Washington, DC.

mythfact.s: You can add cash to some cards at a machine.
mythfact.why: Station machines often take cash or cards.

mythfact.s: You must show the card to the driver and wait.
mythfact.why: You usually tap it on the reader and walk in.

compare.br: In Brazil, many cities have their own transit card (São Paulo has the Bilhete Único), and you can often recharge it at a booth or an app.
compare.us: In the USA each region has its own card, and you can often add money at a machine or online.
compare.tip: Check your balance before you travel so you do not have a problem at the reader.
compare.ask: How much money do you usually add to your card? Say it in English.

quiz.q: The clerk asks “Cash or card?” You want to pay cash. You say…
How do you use a transit card?

pages.title: Reading quest — Nina’s first transit card · part 1
text: Nina arrived in San Francisco on Monday. She wanted to ride the bus, but she did not have a transit card. She walked to a small shop near the station and said, “**Hi! I need a transit card.**”

“**Sure. How much do you want to add?**” the clerk asked. Nina counted her money. “**Twenty dollars, please**,” she said. “**Cash or card?**” “**Cash. Here you go**,” she answered and gave him a twenty-dollar bill.

The clerk put the card in a machine and added the money. Then he said, “**Here’s your card and your change**.” Nina looked at the change in her hand. There were a few coins because the card cost a little.

pages.title: Reading quest — Nina’s first transit card · part 2
text: “**How do I use it?**” she asked. “**Tap it on the reader**,” he said. “It makes a small sound when it works.” Nina put the card in her bag and said, “**Have a nice day!**”
At the bus stop, she tapped the card on the reader. It made a short sound, and a green light came on. Nina smiled. She did not need coins, and she did not need to ask the driver for help.
Later, she told her friend, “A transit card is easy. You tap and go!” Nina felt more at home in the city.
